KNOWN-BAD: A LITERAL NAMING v2 WHILE v3 IS THE HEAD IS REFUSED BY NAME, with the head it should have named. ***This is the shape found three times in one day -- a module reading bars nobody is running under, with the superseding version right beside it on disk***
checks.detail: live/pm_research/pins_v2.py:2 names x_declaration_v2.json, head is x_declaration_v3.json

checks.check: AND THE SAME MODULE PINNING THE HEAD ADMITS -- the census answers about the PIN, not about the module

R-657 -- A LITERAL NAMING A NON-HEAD IS ADMISSIBLE ONLY WHERE THE CODE MARKS IT, and the census READS the marker. ***Two of this census's first hits were not pins at all: a runner's `SUPERSEDED_PARAMS_REL` names the superseded file ON PURPOSE (it IS the guard) and a `_bad_pin` is a known-bad -- a census that cannot tell a PIN from a GUARD reports the guard as the defect it exists to prevent.*** An IDENTIFIER carrying `superseded` as a `_`-token MARKS and is admitted with its reason; a function named `known_bad_*` marks a literal inside it; and the SAME literal in a plainly-named function is REFUSED
AND A MARKER ON A **HEAD** LITERAL IS ADMITTED AND **NOTED**: the marker EXPLAINS a deliberate non-head, it does not GRANT one, so the census reports it rather than treating the word as a licence
checks.detail: the rule is stated in the receipt as a marker on a HEAD literal is admitted and NOTED; the marker explains a deliberate non-hea…

checks.check: REV 71 4.3 -- THE FIRST GATE IS DATAFLOW, and it disposes of the shapes a regex cannot tell apart. ***The reviewer's naive version found ELEVEN pairs and most were false: a `params_v999` known-bad, a declaration module naming its OWN chain, a dead constant, comments.*** Driven on all of them at once: PROSE, a `supersedes` chain entry, a DEAD constant and a `refuses(...)` fixture are all NOT PINS -- only the literal that actually reaches `Path(...).read_text()` is
checks.detail: 5 literals in the noise module -> 1 pin: x_declaration_v3.json in real_pin; the rest are ['MARKED_AND_NOT_A_PIN', 'NOT_A_PIN__IN_A_SUPERSESSION_FIELD', 'NOT_A_PIN__NO_OPEN']

literal_census.the_first_gate_is_dataflow: a literal is a PIN only when it FLOWS INTO A FILE OPEN -- `Path()`/`open`/`read_text`/`read_bytes`/`json.load`, directly or through ONE assignment. A supersession chain entry and a `refuses(...)` fixture are excluded BY CONSTRUCTION. The marker rule (R-657) is the SECOND gate

the_marker_rule.a_marker_is_not_a_licence: a marker on a HEAD literal is admitted and NOTED; the marker explains a deliberate non-head, it does not grant one
the_marker_rule.allowlist: declarations/<seat>_nonhead_allowlist_v*.json, owned by the seat, one reason per entry
the_marker_rule.matched: on `_`-separated TOKENS of the assigned identifier, never as a substring: `SUPERSEDED_PARAMS_REL` marks, `PARAMS_REL` does not

literal_census.why: a pin that names a superseded declaration reads bars nobody is running under -- and the superseding version is right beside it on disk
